## Intent

**Problem:** `waypoint install` currently writes only a placeholder for each of the 4 role-prompt files (`<!-- ${role} role prompt — generated by \`waypoint install\`; content populated by Epic 4. -->`) — no agent pointed at one of `roles/planner.md`/`architect.md`/`implementer.md`/`reviewer.md` has any real guidance for that role.

**Approach:** Replace all 4 placeholders with real, generated content — one function per role, following the same embedded-TypeScript-string convention `renderAgentsMd()`/`renderPatchSpec()`/`renderFeatureSpec()`/`renderSystemPrd()` already use. Each role prompt references the tier commands and gate/verify conventions Epic 1–3 already shipped, stays usable as a system prompt or slash-command body, and — like `AGENTS.md` — never instructs or references invoking `approve`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `packages/core/src/templates/roles.ts` (new) exports one function per role — `renderPlannerPrompt()`, `renderArchitectPrompt()`, `renderImplementerPrompt()`, `renderReviewerPrompt()` — each returning a standalone markdown string usable as a system prompt or slash-command body. One shared file (not 4 separate files) since the 4 roles share enough common framing (tier/gate/verify conventions) that splitting them would duplicate that framing 4 times; this mirrors how `agents-md.ts` is itself one multi-section file rather than 3 separate ones.
- Each role's content is scoped to what that role actually does, all grounded in commands/conventions Epic 1–3 already shipped (no invented mechanism):
  - **Planner**: helps a human/agent pick the right tier (Patch/Feature/System) for a change and draft the initial spec via `new-patch`/`new-feature`/`new-system`, using the same tier heuristics `AGENTS.md`'s Tier Selection section states.
  - **Architect**: for Feature/System-tier work, helps design a spec's Design/architecture content and (System tier only) its phased task breakdown, referencing `waypoint update` for keeping a spec's delta history in sync with the ledger as design decisions are made.
  - **Implementer**: does the actual coding work against an already-drafted spec, referencing `waypoint verify <spec-id> <task-id>` as the sole way a task's `done` status gets recorded, and the pre-commit `gate` check that blocks a Feature/System-tier change with no accompanying spec delta.
  - **Reviewer**: reviews a completed change against its spec, referencing `waypoint check-drift` to catch stale path/symbol references and `waypoint verify`'s ledger as the source of truth for what's actually been verified done — never re-implements or hand-edits ledger fields itself.
- None of the 4 prompts ever use the literal word "approve" anywhere in their content — matching `agents-md.ts`'s own established discipline (using "approval"/"approved" prose forms where the concept needs mentioning, never the bare command verb) so a section-scoped or whole-document check for the word never needs cleverness to stay both correct and non-fragile.
- `scaffold.ts`'s `rolePlaceholder()` function and its single `for (const role of ROLE_NAMES)` plan-entry loop are updated to call the matching new render function per role instead of the placeholder — no changes to the plan-entry mechanism, the preserve-on-reinstall check, or any other part of `scaffold()`. That generic "already exists → preserved untouched" logic already covers these 4 paths; this story adds no new preserve/detection code, exactly as Story 4.1 didn't for `AGENTS.md`.

**Ask First:** none anticipated — each role's scope is grounded directly in the commands/conventions already shipped in Epic 1–3, not a multi-way design fork.

**Never:**
- Mention or instruct invoking `approve` in any of the 4 prompts — the exclusion holds in role-prompt content, not just in `AGENTS.md`'s action list (epics.md AC2).
- Change `scaffold()`'s reinstall/preserve behavior, its plan-entry data shape, `ROLE_NAMES`, or any other scaffolded path's content.
- Invent a new role beyond the 4 already named (Planner, Architect, Implementer, Reviewer) or a new mechanism (e.g. a bespoke multi-agent runtime) — FR10 is explicit that plain markdown files any agent can be pointed at is the whole point, not a runtime.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Fresh install | No pre-existing role files | All 4 `roles/*.md` files are written with their matching `render*Prompt()`'s real content | N/A |
| Content shape | Each `render*Prompt()`'s output | Standalone markdown, plain prose/headings/lists, references at least one real `waypoint` command relevant to that role; never contains the literal word "approve" | N/A |
| Reinstall, user-customized role file | A pre-existing, hand-edited `roles/architect.md` | Preserved byte-for-byte, not regenerated (existing generic `scaffold()` behavior, unchanged by this story) | N/A |
| Reinstall, untouched role file | A pre-existing role file written by a prior install (placeholder or real content) | Preserved byte-for-byte — same "already exists" rule applies regardless of what the content actually is | N/A |

- Given any role-prompt file already exists and has been user-customized, when `waypoint install` runs again, then the existing file is preserved, not regenerated over

Verification-gap found nothing further to fix (a clean pass); edge-case-hunter found the same class of gap already deferred for Story 4.1 (see below); adversarial found nine real, confirmed issues, all patched:
  - **Factually wrong claim in the Architect prompt.** It said `waypoint update` syncs `### MODIFIED`/`### REMOVED` bullets into the ledger alongside `### ADDED` ones — the real implementation only ever syncs `### ADDED` bullets (matching `program.ts`'s own command description and `update-spec.ts`'s actual behavior; `MODIFIED`/`REMOVED` reconciliation is a deliberate manual judgment call for MVP, per Story 2.1's own AC). Fixed the prompt's wording to be accurate.
  - **Both the Planner's and Implementer's closing lines unconditionally stated "approval is a human-only step," contradicting the Planner's own Tier heuristics** (Patch tier has "No approval gate" at all). Fixed both to scope the statement to Feature/System work and explicitly note Patch-tier work has no approval step.
  - **The Reviewer prompt never referenced `waypoint gate --ci --base <ref>`'s done-claim-correctness check**, even though the Reviewer's own stated job (judging whether the ledger's verified-done state matches the diff) is exactly what that check already automates. Added a cross-reference so the Reviewer treats it as a second, automated evidence source rather than re-deriving the same judgment from scratch.
  - **The Implementer's gate-rejection guidance never named the actual mechanism (`waypoint update <spec-id>`)** to resolve a rejection — left an agent without a procedural path if it didn't also have the Architect prompt loaded. Fixed by naming the command explicitly in both the "Your job" bullet and "Gate awareness" section.
  - **Case-sensitivity gap in every `approve`-exclusion test**, in both `roles.test.ts` and `role-prompts-wiring.test.ts` — a future capitalized "Approve" would have silently passed the FR8 guard entirely. Fixed by lowercasing content before every such assertion.
  - **The Implementer's "references the `gate` check" test was trivially satisfied by the unrelated prose phrase "verified-by-gate"**, regardless of whether the actual `gate` command was ever mentioned. Tightened to match the backtick-quoted command form specifically, in both test files.
  - **`scaffold.test.ts`'s inline comment on the role-file assertion loop misdescribed the code beneath it** (claimed to avoid a raw string comparison, then did exactly that). Corrected the comment to accurately describe both checks actually being made — a role-specific heading-marker check and an exact-equality check confirming `ROLE_RENDERERS` wires each role to the correct function.
  - **No test guarded against cross-role content contamination** — all 4 render functions live in one file with near-identical shapes, a real copy-paste risk. Added negative/exclusivity assertions per role (e.g. the Planner prompt must never mention `check-drift`/`waypoint verify`/`waypoint update`), scoped carefully to still allow the Architect's own deliberate `new-feature` escalation cross-reference (added in the same patch round) without false-flagging it.
  - **The Architect's Patch-escalation guidance gave no actionable next step** for the exact "a Patch turns out to need design work" scenario the Planner's own guidance anticipates as "normal and cheap." Added a concrete next step (draft a new Feature spec via `waypoint new-feature <name>`).
  - Deferred to `deferred-work.md`: pre-existing installs (from before this story) keeping the old role-prompt placeholders forever, due to Story 1.1's own unmodified preserve-on-reinstall rule — the same class of gap already deferred for Story 4.1's `AGENTS.md`, for the same reasons.
  - Rejected: the Reviewer's "call out clearly" output guidance being vague about exact channel/consumer (none of the other 3 roles specify an exact output channel either, and prescribing one would overstate this role's authority into a team-specific workflow decision); a prompt-length/token-budget tripwire test (no other template in this codebase has one, and there's no principled basis yet for the right bound).
  - Re-verified after every fix: `npm test` (21 test files, 358 tests, 0 failures — `roles.test.ts` grew from 13 to 17 cases), `npm run build` (clean). I independently read every changed file against each patch before accepting the implementation.

## Design Notes

One shared `roles.ts` file (not 4 separate files, one per role) was chosen over strictly mirroring `patch.ts`/`feature.ts`/`system.ts`'s one-file-per-tier pattern: those 3 tiers have almost no shared framing text (each is a genuinely different frontmatter+body shape), whereas the 4 roles share enough common grounding (the same tier heuristics, the same `verify`/`gate`/`check-drift` conventions, the same approve-exclusion discipline) that 4 separate files would either duplicate that framing 4 times or need their own shared-constants file anyway. `agents-md.ts` already established the "one file, multiple related sections/functions" shape for exactly this kind of case.
